segment_reference_payload.description: Segment's Google Cloud Function destination delivers event data by invoking a Google Cloud Function via an HTTP POST trigger. The function URL is configured in the Segment destination settings, and the full event JSON is sent as the HTTP request body. Authentication is handled through the destination settings when required.
segment_reference_payload.integration_method: HTTP POST to Cloud Function URL (HTTP trigger)

authentication.method: Optional — Google Cloud IAM / OAuth2 identity token

config_fields.functionUrl: The HTTPS URL of the deployed Google Cloud Function
config_fields.credentials: Google Cloud service account credentials JSON for authenticated invocations
config_fields.requireAuthentication: Boolean flag indicating whether authenticated invocations are required

http_trigger.payload_format: Raw event JSON — full Segment event object serialized as JSON body
http_trigger.url_source: Configured in Segment destination settings as the function URL

rudderstack_expected_payload.description: RudderStack's Google Cloud Function destination invokes the configured function URL via an HTTP POST request. The JSON event payload is sent as the raw request body with Content-Type application/json. Optional OAuth2 ID token authentication is supported via Google service account credentials with configurable token caching (default 55-minute timeout). Timeouts are treated as accepted deliveries (HTTP 202).

connection.timeout_behavior: Timeouts are treated as accepted deliveries — returns HTTP 202 / Success

destination_config.credentials: Google Cloud service account credentials JSON (used only when requireAuthentication is true)

authentication.token_caching: Tokens are cached on the Config struct; regenerated when TokenTimeout (default 55 minutes) expires
authentication.token_check_flow: Config.shouldGenerateToken() checks RequireAuthentication flag and TokenTimeout expiration before each Produce call

rudderstack_expected_payload.input_data_format: json.RawMessage — raw JSON event bytes passed directly as HTTP request body

unreachable_function.message: [GOOGLE_CLOUD_FUNCTION] error :: Function call was not executed <network_error>

function_url.segment: Configured in Segment destination settings as the Cloud Function URL
function_url.rudderstack: Configured in destination config as 'googleCloudFunctionUrl' — mapped to Config.FunctionUrl via JSON tag
function_url.parity: Functionally equivalent — both configure the target HTTP endpoint URL

payload_envelope.segment: Raw event JSON — the Segment event object is sent directly as the HTTP POST body
payload_envelope.rudderstack: Raw event JSON (json.RawMessage) — the RudderStack event object is sent directly as the HTTP POST body
payload_envelope.parity: Both send the event as a JSON HTTP POST body; RudderStack events include additional envelope fields (rudderId, originalTimestamp, sentAt, receivedAt)

event_envelope_fields.parity: RudderStack adds rudderId, originalTimestamp, sentAt, receivedAt to the event envelope. The Cloud Function receives these extra fields in the JSON body.

content_type.rudderstack: application/json (set via req.Header.Set in Produce method)

authentication.segment: Configurable authentication via destination settings — supports Google Cloud IAM identity tokens
authentication.rudderstack: Optional OAuth2 ID token authentication via Config.RequireAuthentication flag. When enabled, uses idtoken.NewTokenSource with service account credentials to generate Bearer tokens. Tokens are cached with a configurable timeout (default 55 minutes via google.cloudfunction.token.timeout config key).
authentication.parity: Both platforms support authenticated invocations using Google Cloud credentials. RudderStack implements token caching with a 55-minute default TTL. Token refresh is checked on every Produce call via Config.shouldGenerateToken().

timeout_handling.segment: Standard HTTP timeout behavior — timeouts are delivery failures
timeout_handling.rudderstack: Timeouts are treated as accepted deliveries (HTTP 202 / Success) — rationale: the Cloud Function may still execute after the HTTP client timeout (1 second default). os.IsTimeout check in Produce method.
timeout_handling.parity: Difference — RudderStack treats timeouts as successful delivery (HTTP 202), while Segment treats timeouts as failures. Cloud Function consumers should handle potential duplicate invocations.

context_library.parity: Different SDK library identifiers — does not affect Cloud Function processing

error_handling.rudderstack: Network errors return HTTP 400/Failure; non-200 responses from function return function's status code/Failure with response body logged; authentication failures return HTTP 401/Failure; timeouts return HTTP 202/Success
error_handling.parity: Difference — RudderStack has explicit error categorization with detailed diagnostic messages. The timeout-as-success behavior is unique to RudderStack.

fields.Credentials: string — Google Cloud service account credentials JSON
fields.RequireAuthentication: bool — whether authenticated invocations are required
fields.FunctionUrl: string — the HTTPS URL of the Cloud Function (JSON tag: googleCloudFunctionUrl)
fields.Token: *oauth2.Token — cached OAuth2 token for authenticated requests
fields.TokenCreatedAt: time.Time — timestamp when the cached token was generated
fields.TokenTimeout: time.Duration — configurable token expiration duration (default 55 minutes)

http_client_config.connection_reuse: Shared http.Client across Produce calls; CloseIdleConnections called on Close()

token_management.method: GetToken(ctx context.Context, functionUrl string, opts ...option.ClientOption) (*oauth2.Token, error)
token_management.caching_strategy: Token and TokenCreatedAt stored on Config struct; shouldGenerateToken() checks RequireAuthentication and TokenTimeout expiration

produce_flow.step_1: Create HTTP POST request to Config.FunctionUrl with jsonData as body
produce_flow.step_3: Check Config.shouldGenerateToken() — if true, call Config.generateToken() to refresh OAuth2 ID token
produce_flow.step_4: If RequireAuthentication and Token is not nil, set Authorization: Bearer <access_token> header
produce_flow.step_5: Execute HTTP request via shared httpClient
produce_flow.step_6: Read response body and close response (defer httputil.CloseResponse)
produce_flow.step_7: Handle errors: os.IsTimeout returns 202/Success; other errors return 400/Failure
produce_flow.step_8: Handle valid responses: 200 returns Success; non-200 returns Failure with body logged

parity_summary.overall_parity_status: Needs Verification — functionally equivalent for basic event delivery; key differences in authentication details, timeout handling, and envelope fields
critical_gaps: Timeout handling semantics differ: RudderStack treats HTTP client timeouts as accepted delivery (202/Success) while Segment treats them as delivery failures requiring retry. Cloud Functions receiving events from both platforms should implement idempotent processing.
RudderStack default HTTP client timeout is 1 second — this is aggressive for Cloud Functions that perform non-trivial processing. Segment may use a longer timeout.
non_critical_differences: RudderStack events include additional envelope fields (rudderId, originalTimestamp, sentAt, receivedAt) in the JSON body. Cloud Functions should tolerate unknown fields.
Context library name differs (analytics.js vs rudder-sdk-js) — this is expected and does not affect Cloud Function processing.
Message ID format differs between platforms — different UUID generation strategies.
RudderStack destination config uses JSON tag 'googleCloudFunctionUrl' while Segment uses settings-based configuration.
parity_summary.functional_equivalence: Both platforms deliver events to Google Cloud Functions via HTTP POST with JSON body and optional OAuth2 authentication. The core payload structure (event type, user identifiers, properties/traits, context) is equivalent. Cloud Functions processing events from both platforms should use the 'type' field for dispatch and tolerate additional envelope fields from RudderStack.

notes: Google Cloud Function shared stream destination. Segment slug: google-cloud-function. RudderStack package: services/streammanager/googlecloudfunction/. Both platforms invoke Cloud Functions via HTTP POST with JSON event payloads. Key parity differences: (1) RudderStack adds rudderId, originalTimestamp, sentAt, receivedAt envelope fields; (2) RudderStack treats HTTP timeouts as accepted delivery (202) while Segment treats them as failures; (3) RudderStack uses OAuth2 ID token authentication with 55-minute token caching via idtoken.NewTokenSource; (4) RudderStack default HTTP client timeout is 1 second. Cloud Functions should implement idempotent processing and tolerate additional envelope fields for cross-platform compatibility.
